Description

In the spinal cord PGD2 inhibits allodynia through DP receptors (Minami 1997). After nerve injury, PGD2 made by microglia causes mechanical allodynia through DP2 on spinal neurons (Kanda 2013).

Colour

Red raises pain, blue relieves it, and olive acts both ways. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block.

DP1 is blue and DP2 red. PGD2 is olive, as it acts both ways.

References

  1. Kanda H, Kobayashi K, Yamanaka H, Noguchi K. COX-1-dependent prostaglandin D2 in microglia contributes to neuropathic pain via DP2 receptor in spinal neurons. Glia. 2013 Jun;61(6):943-56. doi: 10.1002/glia.22487. PMID: 23505121.
  2. Minami T, Okuda-Ashitaka E, Nishizawa M, Mori H, Ito S. Inhibition of nociceptin-induced allodynia in conscious mice by prostaglandin D2. Br J Pharmacol. 1997 Oct;122(4):605-10. doi: 10.1038/sj.bjp.0701421. PMID: 9375954.
